newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan December gold imports up 91.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan December gold imports up 91.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's imports of gold bars, coins and plate leapt to 6.908 tonnes in December, a 91.6 percent rise from 3.606 tonnes a year earlier, the Finance Ministry said on Tuesday.
The figure also surpassed November's 6.791 tonnes.
The ministry said Taiwan's gold exports in December remained modest at 0.307 tonnes, up from 0.271 tonnes in December 1995.
Traders attributed the December import jump to falling world gold prices and the local market's exhaustion of excess stocks that had piled up in early 1996.

Taiwan's gold market was saturated by record gold imports in March, when acute military tensions with arch-rival China sparked a run on U.S. dollars and panic buying of gold by Taiwan people seeking a safe haven.
Taiwan imported a record 25.238 tonnes of gold in March alone, a 162.4 percent jump compared with March 1995.
Taiwan gold dealers said supplies accumulated in early 1996 had been consumed by late November, enabling demand to return to normal in December.
Despite the March panic, Taiwan's imports of gold bars, coins and plate in all of 1996 actually fell 13.59 percent to 95.655 tonnes from 110.696 tonnes in 1995, the ministry data showed.
Gold traders attributed the 1996 full-year import drop to continuted sluggishness in Taiwan's economy.
January imports are expected to increase due to low international gold prices at a time of traditionally strong demand -- the Lunar New Year holiday that falls on February 7 this year.
